title: Israel’s Election Leaves Netanyahu in Limbo

notes.headline: Israel Election Deadlock and Potential Iran Conflict Heighten Geopolitical Risks Post-US Midterms
notes.summary: Israel's election resulted in no clear majority for Prime Minister Netanyahu or the opposition, potentially leading to months of political instability. This deadlock occurs as regional tensions with Iran are expected to intensify following the US midterm elections, with possibilities of joint Israel-US military action. Such geopolitical uncertainty could impact global energy markets and risk sentiment.
key_takeaways: Neither Netanyahu's Likud nor the opposition block secured a majority in the 120-seat parliament.
President Isaac Herzog will consult parties to determine who can form a coalition, a process that could take months.
Netanyahu's political survival is tied to his image as a security leader despite the October 7th failures.
Arab parties won a record 19 seats, complicating traditional coalition dynamics.
Ethan Bronner suggests a potential for military action against Iran after the US midterms, with a 10% chance before.
A military emergency could force a national unity government between Netanyahu and opposition leaders like Gantz and Bennett.
macro: Geopolitics: Political deadlock in Israel and potential for regional war with Iran.
Geopolitics: US-Israel military cooperation and its impact on Middle East stability.
priced_in: Expectations of a difficult path for any party trying to form a government in Israel.
Anticipation of increased military activity in the Middle East following the US midterm elections.
fundamentals: Crude Oil: Supply risks associated with potential military strikes on Iran or retaliatory actions.

assets.view: Potential for military operations against Iran could disrupt supply and drive prices higher.
Increased geopolitical risk and potential for regional war favor safe-haven assets.
Geopolitical instability in the Middle East typically weighs on global risk appetite.

guests.name: Ethan Bronner
guests.role: Israel Bureau Chief & Senior Mideast Editor, Bloomberg News
guests.key_view: Netanyahu faces a difficult path to a 61-seat majority, and the regional focus is shifting toward a potential conflict with Iran after the US midterms.

title: Bolsonaro Leaves Brazil After Rejecting Election

notes.headline: Brazilian assets plunge as Lula victory triggers re-pricing of fiscal policy expectations
notes.summary: Following Lula da Silva's presidential victory over Jair Bolsonaro, Brazilian markets experienced a massive sell-off as investors recalibrated for a shift from pro-market fiscal policies to pro-social programs. The Brazilian Real saw its worst one-day drop since 1999, and the stock exchange triggered circuit breakers for the first time since the pandemic. The political situation remains volatile as Bolsonaro has fled to the United States and refused to formally concede the election.
key_takeaways: Brazilian markets saw a massive sell-off on Monday following the election results.
The Brazilian Real dropped nearly 10% in a single day, the worst performance since 1999.
The Brazilian stock exchange hit circuit breakers for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic.
Investors are unwinding bets on Bolsonaro's pro-market fiscal adjustments and debt management.
Bolsonaro has landed in the US and stated he will lead the opposition from abroad.
The sell-off is viewed as a re-adjustment from the rally seen after the first round of voting.
Hedge funds were significantly impacted by the sudden reversal in market sentiment.
macro: Geopolitics: Political transition in Brazil and Bolsonaro's refusal to recognize election results.
Fiscal Policy: Shift from Bolsonaro's pro-market stance to Lula's pro-social program narrative.
Emerging Markets: Significant volatility in BRL and Brazilian ADRs impacting broader EM sentiment.
priced_in: Markets had priced in a high probability of a Bolsonaro victory or momentum following the first round of voting.
The current sell-off represents a 're-adjustment' of expectations regarding Brazil's debt levels and fiscal costs.
fundamentals: Fiscal adjustments and the level of Brazil's indebtedness are the primary concerns for institutional investors.
Lula's focus on pro-social programs is perceived as a risk to fiscal discipline compared to the previous administration.

assets.view: Experienced its worst one-day drop since 1999, falling close to 10%.
Hit circuit breakers on Monday following a massive sell-off.
US-listed Brazilian assets were part of the broader market sell-off and re-pricing.

guests.name: Filipe Pacheco
guests.key_view: The market crash is a direct result of investors re-adjusting from the pro-market expectations set during the first round of the election.

catalysts: Bolsonaro's potential leadership of the opposition from the US.
Lula's upcoming announcements regarding fiscal policy and cabinet appointments.

title: Midterm Fight Comes Down to the Final Days

notes.headline: US Midterm Elections Point to Potential House Flip and Increased Political Gridlock
notes.summary: The final countdown to the US midterm elections suggests a high probability of the House of Representatives flipping to Republican control, while the Senate remains a toss-up. Analysts discuss how a divided government would likely lead to a wave of congressional investigations and oversight into the administration's spending and personnel. Record-breaking early voting turnout, particularly in states like South Carolina, adds significant uncertainty to the final results.
key_takeaways: The House of Representatives is widely expected to flip to Republican control.
Senate control remains the primary uncertainty with key races in Alaska, Ohio, and the Carolinas.
A Republican-led House is expected to initiate aggressive oversight and potential impeachment proceedings.
Early voting is seeing massive surges, with South Carolina reporting an 83% increase over two years ago.
Donald Trump remains a polarizing but powerful driver of voter turnout for the Republican party.
Campaign financing has reached unprecedented levels, including significant 'AI spend' and donor activity from figures like Elon Musk.
macro: Fiscal gridlock is anticipated if the House flips, likely stalling major legislative agendas.
Increased geopolitical oversight is expected, specifically regarding foreign relations and administration spending.
Potential for administrative instability due to promised congressional investigations and impeachment attempts.
priced_in: Market consensus largely expects a Republican takeover of the House.
The Senate outcome is not fully priced in due to tight polling and high early-voter variability.
fundamentals: Massive campaign spending is noted, with Joe Mathieu highlighting 'AI spend' that is difficult to quantify.
Democratic candidates are raising significant cash, described as 'ATMs' for the party.

assets.view: Historical preference for gridlock may be offset by the threat of aggressive congressional investigations and administrative instability.
Significant 'AI spend' in the political cycle highlights sector relevance, though regulatory outlook remains tied to House control.
Fiscal gridlock typically limits large-scale deficit spending, which can have a stabilizing effect on long-term rates.

notes.headline: AI backlash and data center resistance emerge as key political risks for tech infrastructure expansion
notes.summary: The discussion centers on the growing bipartisan backlash against AI, specifically regarding the construction of data centers and fears of job displacement. Local resistance to infrastructure is becoming a significant election issue, with some states like New York already issuing moratoriums. Despite these hurdles, experts argue that building AI capacity is a national security imperative to compete with China, likely leading to increased federal regulation and global standards.

New York has issued the first statewide moratorium on hyperscale data centers.
AI-aligned political groups have spent $56 million on elections to counter the backlash.
250,000 jobs in information services have been lost since the advent of ChatGPT, fueling voter anxiety.
CEOs and industry leaders are increasingly calling for a federal regulatory regime similar to the FAA for AI.
The tech race with China makes the continued build-out of AI infrastructure a strategic necessity despite local opposition.

Labor: Significant job losses in the information services sector (250k) are driving political sentiment.

notes.headline: Rising women's sports popularity drives stadium infrastructure upgrades and significant renovation spending
notes.summary: The surge in viewership and attendance for women's professional sports is forcing stadiums to rethink infrastructure, particularly restroom capacity. New plumbing codes are shifting towards a 2:1 ratio of women's to men's facilities to accommodate longer wait times and changing demographics. This trend is leading to significant capital expenditure for renovations and the development of purpose-built stadiums for women's teams.
key_takeaways: Women's sports viewership and attendance are skyrocketing in the U.S., creating new infrastructure demands.
Stadiums are adopting a 2:1 ratio for women's restroom space in updated plumbing codes to reduce wait times.

Purpose-built stadiums for women's sports are emerging, such as the Kansas City Current's NWSL stadium.
Scheduling conflicts at multi-use arenas highlight the growing need for dedicated women's sports venues.

title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed

notes.summary: The segment highlights unexpected business resilience in the retail and consumer sectors despite trade tensions and supply chain hurdles. Spirit Halloween doubled its business since 2019 despite heavy tariffs on Chinese imports by optimizing operations rather than raising prices. Additionally, high-volume consumer brands like Home Depot and Cheesecake Factory continue to see strong demand for niche and high-margin products, signaling robust US consumer health.

Retailers managed trade war costs through 'war rooms' and capital spending freezes instead of immediate price hikes.

Cheesecake Factory is identified as the highest-grossing major restaurant chain by average unit volume.
General Mills (Cheerios) is implementing packaging changes (Ziploc seals) to address long-standing consumer friction and maintain brand loyalty.

title: Burger King US President on Sales Turnaround

notes.headline: Burger King sees sales growth as stressed consumers treat fast food as an affordable reward
notes.summary: Tom Curtis, President of Burger King US & Canada, discusses the chain's 8.3% comp sales growth, which significantly outperformed analyst estimates. The turnaround is attributed to operational improvements, store remodels, and a focus on core products like the Whopper. Despite a consumer base described as 'stressed' by inflation in both the US and Canada, Burger King is gaining market share from competitors by positioning itself as a high-quality reward rather than engaging in a 'race to the bottom' on value.
key_takeaways: 3Q comp sales grew 8.3%, beating the 6.21% estimate.
Burger King has surpassed Wendy's to become the #2 burger chain in the US.
Consumers are viewed as 'stressed' but are treating fast food as an affordable luxury or reward.
The company is raising prices less this year than in previous years to maintain value perception.
Store remodels (60% complete) are providing mid-single-digit traffic uplifts.
Nugget sales increased 35% following a quality-focused relaunch.
The Canadian consumer is noted as being potentially more stressed by inflation than the US consumer.
macro: Consumer Health: US and Canadian consumers described as 'stressed' over the last three years.
Inflation: Higher inflation in Canada is impacting consumer sentiment more severely than in the US.
priced_in: Comp sales growth of 6.21% was the market consensus before the 8.3% beat.
fundamentals: Restaurant Brands International (QSR) 3Q performance.
Franchisee P&L health is the primary driver for the pace of store remodels.
Market share shift: Growth is likely coming at the expense of closest competitors like McDonald's and Wendy's.

assets.view: Strong comp sales and market share gains for a major component of the consumer discretionary sector.

title: Democratic Wave in House Looks Likely, Cook's Covey Says

notes.headline: Democrats projected to gain 12-25 House seats amid emerging bipartisan AI regulation consensus
notes.summary: Erin Covey of The Cook Political Report discusses the shifting US political landscape, predicting a Democratic wave in the House with gains of 12-25 seats. The discussion highlights how sagging approval ratings for Donald Trump are impacting Republican candidates even in deep red states like Texas. For markets, the most significant development is the emerging bipartisan consensus on regulating data centers and AI, alongside expectations of continued legislative gridlock.
key_takeaways: Democrats are projected to pick up 12-25 seats in the House, potentially giving them a majority.
Trump's sagging approval ratings are acting as a drag on Republican candidates in competitive and red-state races.
The Texas Senate race is increasingly competitive, with Democrats seen as slight favorites in some polling.
Bipartisan consensus is emerging regarding the regulation of data centers and AI industry funding.
Expectations of legislative gridlock remain high for the next two years regardless of the election outcome.
Progressive proposals include public ownership stakes in AI firms like OpenAI and Anthropic.
macro: Fiscal/Political: Potential shift in House majority to Democrats could lead to increased legislative gridlock.
Growth: Potential for sector-specific headwinds in the technology space due to new regulatory frameworks.
fundamentals: Technology: Bipartisan support for data center regulation and scrutiny of AI industry super PACs.
AI: Proposals for 50% public ownership of major AI firms like OpenAI and Anthropic mentioned as a progressive goal.

assets.view: Potential for increased regulation of data centers and AI firms could pressure tech valuations.
